name: Shual
overview: Shual was a male member of the tribe of Asher, identified uniquely as the son of Zophah according to 1 Chronicles 7:36. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide additional details about his life or role. His mention serves primarily to establish genealogical records within the tribe of Asher.
namesAndTitles: The name Shual is a proper name meaning "fox or jackal," as noted in 1 Chronicles 7:36. This meaning is given without indication that the name was divinely assigned. The name reflects a common Hebrew personal name without further elaboration in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Shual is explicitly identified as the son of Zophah in Scripture, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 7:36. No other family relationships are documented for him in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Shual's significance lies in his inclusion within the genealogical listings of the tribe of Asher, which helps preserve the lineage and tribal identity important to Israel's history. His mention supports the biblical emphasis on family lines and tribal heritage, foundational for understanding God's covenant people. Though not a prominent figure in narrative events, his record contributes to the comprehensive biblical genealogies.
